topic: UX Strategy, Product Thinking, and Design Handoff
learningObjectives: Connect UX decisions with user needs and product objectives.
Prepare designs and specifications for development handoff.
Communicate design decisions clearly to cross-functional teams.

activities.title: UX Strategy Map
activities.instruction: Explore how user needs, product objectives, constraints, and outcomes connect.

content.concept: UX strategy aligns user needs, business objectives, product constraints, and measurable outcomes.
content.tip: Select each element to understand how it influences design decisions.

items.label: User Needs
items.description: The problems, goals, expectations, and behaviors the product should address.

items.label: Product Goals
items.description: The outcomes the product or organization wants to achieve.

items.label: Constraints
items.description: Technical, business, time, regulatory, or resource limitations.

items.label: UX Decisions
items.description: Design choices that balance user needs with product goals and constraints.

items.label: Success Metrics
items.description: Measures used to evaluate whether the experience achieves its intended outcomes.

activities.title: Product Decision Matcher
activities.instruction: Match product situations with the UX decision that best addresses them.

content.concept: Design decisions should consider user value, product goals, technical constraints, and available evidence.
content.tip: Consider both user impact and product context when evaluating a design decision.

pairs.prompt: Users cannot find the most important task on the homepage.
A feature has high user value but requires infrastructure that is unavailable for the current release.
Research shows users misunderstand an important action label.
A proposed feature has no evidence of solving the target problem.
pairs.answer: Validate the problem and value first

pairs.prompt: A successful experience needs to be measured after launch.

choices: Validate the problem and value first

activities.title: Developer Handoff Builder
activities.instruction: Assemble the essential information required for a clear design handoff.

content.concept: A useful handoff communicates layouts, dimensions, states, assets, interactions, responsive behavior, and design tokens.
content.tip: A developer should be able to understand what to build, how it behaves, and what values or assets to use.

activities.title: Handoff Completeness Check
activities.instruction: Identify the missing information that could create implementation ambiguity.

content.concept: Complete handoff documentation reduces ambiguity between designers and developers during implementation.
content.tip: Look for missing states, dimensions, responsive behavior, interaction rules, assets, and design tokens.

scenarios.question: A button design shows only its default appearance. What important information is missing?
scenarios.explanation: Developers need to know how the button behaves in hover, focus, disabled, loading, and active states when applicable.

scenarios.question: A desktop layout is provided but no information explains how it should behave on mobile.
scenarios.explanation: Responsive behavior should explain how the design changes across screen sizes.

scenarios.question: An interface uses icons but no source files or specifications are provided.
scenarios.explanation: Developers need the correct assets or a clear reference for obtaining them.

scenarios.question: Spacing values are inconsistent and no token system is documented.
scenarios.explanation: Documented tokens help developers reproduce the intended spacing and visual system consistently.
